clues: This city sits in the centre of its country. Hills and high land ring it, and a low valley looks out toward the Adriatic Sea.
It is one of the wettest cities in Europe, yet also one of the sunniest. It gets more than two thousand hours of sun each year.
It was founded in 1614 by Sylejman Pasha Bargjini. He was an Ottoman nobleman, and the Old Mosque stood at its heart.
People have lived on this site without a break since the Iron Age. It was likely the heart of a kingdom of the Illyrian people.
To the east, Dajti rises up over the land. This is the capital of Albania, and its largest city too.
